description of a reference material and its characterisation: 12 sequencing and mapping technologies applied to the same DNA, each with its own library preparation, pipeline and per-technology validation statistics
quote: The NIST Reference Material DNA has been characterized to an unprecedented degree. We have collected a large diverse set of data from 12 sequencing technologies and library preparation methods ( Table 1 ). These data include high-depth paired-end short read whole genome sequencing (WGS) and whole exome sequencing (WES), long mate-pair WGS, pseudo long read (‘read clouds’) WGS, long read WGS, genome mapping, and exome sequencing.

The data come from 12 technologies: BioNano Genomics, Complete Genomics paired-end and LFR, Ion Proton exome, Oxford Nanopore, Pacific Biosciences, SOLiD, 10X Genomics GemCode WGS, and Illumina exome and WGS paired-end, mate-pair, and synthetic long reads.
